messages:
Maya Chen: Quick preflight for the Apr 28 webinar + launch posts — can SEO folks confirm keywords, schema, internal links, redirects, and inbound routing before we publish? Timeline: content freeze 2026-04-20, deploy 2026-04-26, webinar 2026-04-28. Owners?
Oliver Park: I can own keywords + redirects. I started a keyword mapping sheet: https://docs.google.com/sheets/d/1EXAMPLE (please don't edit until I tag you). Top targets: "Redwood inference pricing", "low-latency LLM inference", "inference cost optimization". Also prioritize long-tails for the webinar: "how to run LLMs cheaply", "inference batching best practices".
Tess Rivera: I'll pair on anchors/internal links and confirm H2/H3s that match those keywords. Want a short anchor list from Oliver so content can wire it in. Also: do we canonicalize the webinar page to the blog post or keep separate?
Oliver Park: Keep the webinar page separate, add rel=canonical to the canonical content-version if there's a written recap to avoid duplication. For the blog recap, canonical -> recap; webinar page should have event schema and link to recap via internal link.
Kai Johnson: I'll own form tracking/lead routing. We need redirect rules for the gated PDF and a consistent UTM pattern. Proposal: add ?utm_source=webinar&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=apr28; after form submit redirect to /thanks?src=webinar. Also want to make sure redirects preserve utm params.
seo-bot: Automated crawl (last run):
 - Duplicate meta description found on /blog/launch and /blog/launch-preview (low severity)
 - 302 detected: /old-pricing -> /pricing (suggest 301)
 - Missing structured data on /events/webinar-apr28 (no event schema)
(see full report: https://internal.example.com/crawl/1769994321)
Oliver Park: Confirming redirects: use 301 for permanent moves (SEO). For temporary A/B we can 302. Example nginx rule we plan to hand to infra:
```nginx
# preserve querystring, permanent redirect
rewrite ^/old-pricing$ /pricing permanent;
rewrite ^/resources/llm-cheatsheet$ /resources/llm-cheatsheet-v2? break; # handled with app-level redirect to keep utms
```
Also: provide a CSV mapping of old->new paths, I'll upload to the sheet.
Amir (Eng): We can push most rules to CDN edge. Prefer 301 via CDN config for scale. Will need the CSV by EOD 2026-04-22. We can also add a querystring-preserve flag; tell us which exact params to keep.
Oliver Park: Params to preserve: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, gclid, ref.
Tess Rivera: For internal linking I'll produce a list of 12 anchors: 6 CTAs to pricing, 4 cross-links to docs (dedicated/private), 2 links to webinar recap. Will upload to the content sheet by 2026-04-18.
Caro (Design): I'll deliver OG image + alt text for the webinar page and blog hero by 2026-04-19. Alt text: "Redwood Inference — webinar: inference cost & latency best practices"
Oliver Park: Schema notes: add Event + FAQ JSON-LD on the webinar page. Minimal event schema: name, startDate, endDate, location, url, description, performer (speaker). FAQ for the recap page with 4 Qs about cost / latency / dedicated vs private / signups.
Maya Chen: Action items recap:
 - Oliver: keyword sheet + CSV redirect map (due 2026-04-22)
 - Tess: anchor text & internal link list (due 2026-04-18)
 - Amir: CDN redirect push (blocked until CSV, target 2026-04-25)
 - Kai: UTM + form redirect flow + inbound routing (due 2026-04-23)
 - Caro: OG image + alt text (due 2026-04-19)
 - Oliver + Amir: decide 301 vs 302 list (meeting Wed 2026-04-22 10:30 PT)
Please reply with :white_check_mark: next to your line when you accept.
Kai Johnson: ✅ I'll own the tracking and confirm the form redirect flow.
Oliver Park: ✅ I'll finish keyword mapping and upload CSV.
Tess Rivera: ✅ noted, will upload anchors 4/18.
Amir (Eng): ✅ will schedule CDN window once CSV is in.
Caro (Design): ✅ on images by 4/19.
Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. Small follow-up: does anyone see a risk with the gated PDF redirect losing referral info? If so we should add a server-side append of utm params before issuing the 301.
Oliver Park: Good call. Best to append on server side then 301 to the final URL so analytics keeps source. Amir, can infra do that in the CDN edge function?
Amir (Eng): Yes, edge function can read query, append if missing, then return 301. We'll mock in staging.
Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll lock the content freeze on 4/20 then. Thanks all!
